# These NBA Roles Will Decide Fantasy Basketball Drafts

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-06-30, 26:50. https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o

## Summary

Josh Lloyd, recording the day before NBA free agency opened, goes through the roster situations that could change fantasy value during the player movement period. He covers three open lead creation roles: Charlotte after the LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges trades, Milwaukee after losing Giannis, and Memphis after losing Ja Morant. He then looks at center situations in Brooklyn, Detroit, the Clippers, Golden State and Boston, and forward situations in Minnesota, the Lakers and Golden State, plus a possible knock-on effect in Washington. His main point is that we think we know the answers in most of these spots, but the teams are still in flux. One trade can change everything, so don't overreact to single moves.

## Rules and methods

- [4:18](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=258) Two signs of a year three or year four star leap are a higher free throw rate and a higher assist rate, even for players who are not point guards.
  > "increase in assist rate even if you're not a point guard."
- [25:49](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1549) Early in free agency, don't overreact to single moves. More trades can change the picture quickly.
  > "And it's why like overreactions to individual moves, yeah, can often lead you astray."
- [18:25](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1105) Per-minute big men pile up numbers, but they only have fantasy value if they get enough minutes. Watch for spots where a lack of depth forces those minutes on them.
  > "just not good enough to get enough minutes usually. But what if they're in a position"
- [17:55](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1075) A late-round big is only worth drafting if he can reach about 30 minutes. If his minutes get split down to around 22, he is useless.
  > "if he's got 30 minute only upside that can push to 22 because they want to split"
